title: User menu
description: Current-user affordance: avatar + dropdown with Profile / Log out and (when allowed) a workspace switcher. Reads `window.wpAdminWorkspaces.user`.

documentation.purpose: Acting-user affordance: avatar trigger that opens a DropdownMenu with three controls (Profile, optional Switch workspace submenu, Log out). All data sourced from `window.wpAdminWorkspaces.user` (displayName, avatarUrl, profileUrl, logoutUrl) + `window.wpAdminWorkspaces.workspaces` (for the switcher submenu). Workspace switcher only renders when more than one `user-switchable` workspace is available; calls `window.wpAdminWorkspaces.switchWorkspace(slug)` which posts the new active workspace + reloads.

reads.purpose: Display name, avatar URL, profile URL, logout URL.
Available workspaces (with `user-switchable` flag) for the switcher submenu.

states.renders: Avatar trigger + dropdown with Profile + Log out.
Same dropdown plus `Switch to {title}` entries between Profile and Log out.

interactions.effect: Call `window.wpAdminWorkspaces.switchWorkspace(slug)` — PHP saves new active workspace + page reloads.

a11y.focus-management: DropdownMenu handles focus trap when open. Avatar has `aria-label={displayName}`.
a11y.screen-reader: Avatar `` carries empty `alt=""` (decorative — the `aria-label` on the toggle is the accessible name).

constraints.note: Doesn't fetch user data via core-data — `wpAdminWorkspaces.user` is injected PHP-side at every page load. Cheaper than a REST round trip; safe because user identity is fixed for the session.

Switching workspaces does a full page reload (PHP-side option write + reload). No SPA-style live switch; the alternative would require unmounting + remounting the entire workspace, which has tricky edge cases (modal state, in-flight saves).
Uses legacy `DropdownMenu` from `@wordpress/components`. WPDS 0.12 has no direct port; `Tabs.*` + `Popover.*` could compose one but `DropdownMenu` is more semantic.
`profileUrl` defaults to `#/profile` if missing. Workspaces that omit a `#/profile` route from their map will render the link, but clicking it 404s.

The `role: "region"` field in this manifest is NOT applied to the rendered DOM. Region wrappers in the kernel read the engine template's `role` and emit `<div role={template.role}>` themselves. The app manifest role is documentation — it advertises the landmark role this app expects its region to carry. Mismatch between manifest role and rendered role indicates the app is mounted in the wrong kind of region.

design-system-leakage.purpose: Avatar trigger + items + submenu — no WPDS 0.12 port.
Fallback trigger icon when no avatar URL.
